title: Dedicated staged rollouts: finalize PRD + launch plan, beta customers, and cross-functional sign-offs
creator: Lauren Bishop
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Goal: drive PRD completion + launch milestones for “Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools”, including beta customer selection and cross-functional sign-offs (SRE/Infra/Security).

Background
Dedicated customers are increasingly blocked by risky pool upgrades (model version bumps, runtime builds, routing policy changes). Today we have basic canaries but they are not first-class for reserved pools, and early experiments have shown capacity-starvation / unexpected 429 failure modes when partitions are too small. This initiative introduces explicit stage plans with measurable gates, deterministic promotion/abort/hold semantics, and auditability.

What this ticket owns (PM work)
1) PRD completion and alignment
- Lock MVP scope for v1 (staged rollout safety, not general experimentation platform).
- Define operator + customer-admin workflows in Console, including “hold/freeze”, “abort/rollback”, and admin-only force overrides.
- Define default stage templates and constraints (esp. for small pools / multi-region pools).
- Define “gates” for promotion (error/latency/saturation/GPU health/OOM/429), plus missing-data behavior and minimum sample size.

2) Launch plan (beta → GA)
- Define milestones, feature-flag strategy, and enablement gates.
- Ensure runbooks, oncall readiness, alerting standards, and change management requirements are met.
- Coordinate comms plan for beta design partners and internal enablement (support/TAM, oncall, release eng).

3) Beta customer selection + success criteria
- Identify 1–2 design partners for limited beta.
- Define beta entry criteria (pool size, region setup, workload patterns, willingness to run staged changes).
- Define “beta success” and “exit to GA” metrics.

Deliverables
- PRD finalized and signed off by Product + Eng + SRE + Infra + Security.
- Written launch plan with dates and explicit sign-off checklist.
- Beta customer list + enablement plan (feature flag scope + support readiness).
- Open-questions list with owners and decision dates.

MVP scope (proposed; confirm in PRD)
In-scope
- DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan: stage definitions, required gates, deterministic promotion/abort/hold.
- Standard gates: error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation/headroom, GPU health, OOM rate, request drop/429.
- Audit logs for all rollout actions, including override reasons.
- Console flow: stage timeline, promote/abort/hold controls, gate evidence panel.

Out-of-scope (v1)
- Arbitrary customer-defined metrics and custom query languages for gates.
- General A/B experimentation beyond gating and safe rollout.

Launch milestones (target)
- Phase 0 (done/near-done): requirements + success criteria (Product/SRE/Infra alignment).
- Phase 1: control plane + routing primitives behind flags; manual gates allowed.
- Phase 2: automated gate evaluation + Console UI + dashboards/alerts.
- Phase 3: dogfood on internal Dedicated pools → limited beta (1–2 customers).
- Phase 4: GA + docs/runbooks + post-launch reliability review.

Proposed beta customers (candidates; finalize with TAM + Sales + SRE)
- Lattice AI (Dedicated prospect; rollout safety called out as blocker).
- EmberSearch (throughput-sensitive embeddings workload; wants zero-downtime model upgrades).
- HarborBank (regulated; strong audit/change-management requirements) — likely later beta/GA depending on security sign-off readiness.

Beta entry criteria (draft)
- Pool capacity: minimum size to support 1% / 10% canary without starving (Infra to confirm final threshold; likely N>=8 GPUs per region or equivalent).
- Regions: prefer single-region reserved pool for initial beta; multi-region only after routing/fallback semantics proven.
- Workload: stable baseline traffic (avoid extremely spiky patterns until gate window + min-sample logic is hardened).
- Customer readiness: named customer admin + oncall contact, agree to maintenance windows and rollback expectations.

Success metrics (draft)
- 0 customer-visible SLO breaches attributable to rollout mechanism during beta (excluding pre-existing fleet issues).
- Mean time to detect gate regression < 10 minutes; mean time to abort/rollback < 5 minutes from decision.
- At least 3 real staged changes executed end-to-end (model version or runtime build) with stage promotions logged and auditable.
- No high-severity telemetry/cardinality incidents from stage-tagging in production.

Cross-functional sign-offs (checklist)
SRE (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes)
- Gate thresholds align to Dedicated SLOs and error budget policy.
- Alerting: page vs ticket routing clarified; no excessive noise.
- Failure modes covered: missing metrics, telemetry lag, region impairment mid-stage, stuck holds.

Infra (Irene Choi / Vanessa Ortiz)
- Partitioning guidelines published (min headroom, per-stage replica sizing).
- Guardrails: prevent over-partitioning small pools; defined behavior for partial capacity / degraded GPUs.

Security/Compliance (Kaitlyn Nguyen + audit logging team)
- RBAC for promote/abort/force-promote/hold; admin-only overrides.
- Audit events schema approved; retention/export compatibility verified.
- Customer-facing visibility rules for overrides confirmed (what is visible to customer admins vs internal-only fields).

Open questions (need decisions)
1) Missing telemetry behavior: fail-closed vs fail-open, per-signal staleness thresholds, and UI messaging. (Owner: Paula Mendes + Logan Wright; decision by 2025-02-14)
2) Default stage templates: 1/10/50/100 vs include 0% warmup stage, and how to represent replica partitions in small pools. (Owner: Marissa Cole + Mina Haddad; decision by 2025-02-18)
3) Force-promote policy: when allowed, required “reason” field, and customer visibility/audit wording. (Owner: Kaitlyn Nguyen + Priya Natarajan; decision by 2025-02-20)
4) Streaming sessions behavior on rollback: pin in-flight requests vs reroute on token boundaries, and implications for customer SLAs. (Owner: Jordan Lee + Vikram Singh; decision by 2025-02-25)

comments: 2025-02-03 (Lauren Bishop): Added customer signal summary and proposed MVP scope. Biggest risk called out: small-pool fragmentation leading to 429s if canary partition is too small. Requesting Infra to provide hard guardrails + validation rules in control plane.

2025-02-10 (Marissa Cole): Console dependencies clarified: need stable gate evidence schema + promotion action availability logic. Design is proceeding with stage timeline component; please lock stage naming defaults ASAP to avoid rework.

2025-02-14 (Priya Natarajan): Decision leaning toward fail-closed on missing metrics with explicit manual override (admin-only) and audit trail. Need SRE to define staleness thresholds and UI to clearly communicate “unknown due to telemetry lag.”

2025-02-18 (Sean Gallagher): SRE asks to tie promotion eligibility to error budget burn (no promote under high burn / active incident). Also requesting minimum sample size enforcement; otherwise p99 is too noisy for low-traffic canaries.

2025-02-20 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Security review notes: force-promote must require a reason string and should emit audit events with actor + IP + request_id + old/new stage. Confirm whether customer admins can see force-promote events in Console audit view (likely yes, with limited fields).

2025-03-05 (Liam O'Rourke): Design partner interest confirmed with EmberSearch and Lattice AI. Both want clear rollback semantics and an explicit “hold” mode for change windows; they are willing to start with Redwood-operated promotions.

2025-03-12 (Talia Benson): Updated milestones and added explicit sign-off checklist. Scheduling beta readiness review with Release Eng + SRE on 3/20; will align on feature flag scope (account + pool + region) before enabling any customer pools.
